newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil asks probe of radio bid-rigging charges.
newsitem.headline: Brazil asks probe of radio bid-rigging charges.

text.p: Brazil's Communications Minister Sergio Motta asked for a probe of allegations that officials took bribes from bidders in the granting of FM radio concessions, a ministry spokesman said.
"All I know is the minister sent a request to the federal police on Friday asking them to investigate," the spokesman said.

He said Motta wants to get to the bottom of allegations in the local press that lawmakers and ministry officials took bribes to assure certain bidders would win public tenders of the radio concessions.

Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper made the allegation last week, saying lawmakers schemed to charge 50,000 reais to 150,000 reais to rig, through ministry accomplices, the bidding process for new concessions.

On Monday, the paper reported it had access to a tape recording made by a businessman revealing that lawmakers and ministry officials also were involved in a scheme to take money to expand existing frequencies.
The reports could not be independently verified.
